description:
Project Overview

This is a fully funded PhD studentship investigating the role of the spliceosome in dominant forms of monogenic male infertility, supervised by Dr Alex Martin-Geary and Dr Margot Wyrwoll.

Research Focus

  • Genetic Analysis: Using whole-genome sequencing data from infertile men
  • Spliceosome Research: Investigating splicing disruptions in male infertility
  • Variant Interpretation: Predicting pathogenicity of genetic variants
  • Functional Testing: Using minigene splicing assays and CRISPR-engineered cell models
  • Transcriptomic Analysis: Analyzing splicing patterns during spermatogenesis

Funding & Benefits

  • Tuition Fees: Full coverage (UK rate) for 3.5-4 years
  • Stipend: £21,805 per year (UKRI rate) for 3.5-4 years
  • Research Costs: Access to genomics and molecular biology facilities
  • Training: Comprehensive training in genetics and bioinformatics

Eligibility Criteria

  • Background in genetics, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, bioinformatics, or related field
  • Strong interest in human genetics and mechanisms of disease
  • Willingness to work across computational and wet-lab approaches
  • Prior laboratory experience in molecular biology
  • Residency: Home-rate students only

Application Process

  1. Visit project page
  2. Follow application instructions
  3. Submit required documents
  4. Shortlisting process
  5. Interview
  6. Award notification
